ideas.title: The Coffee Price Trap
ideas.angle: The viewer is presented with 3 prices and forced to pick the 'best deal' in 3 seconds; this reveals the Decoy Effect where the middle option exists only to make the most expensive one look like a bargain. Comment trigger: Ask viewers if they fell for the 'Medium' trap.
ideas.reason: Interactive 'choice' videos have the highest retention because they force the viewer to engage mentally before the reveal. The Decoy Effect is a proven viral psychological concept used by Starbucks and Apple.
sources: Dan Ariely - Predictably Irrational (Decoy Effect research)
Journal of Consumer Research - Asymmetric Dominance Effect

ideas.title: The 3-Word Negotiator
ideas.angle: Shows a social power hack where repeating the last 3 words of a seller's sentence forces them to lower prices or reveal secrets through the 'Mirroring' effect. Forces viewers to visualize their last negotiation. Subscribe trigger: 'Use this to save thousands.'
ideas.reason: Social power moves and 'FBI level' negotiation tactics are currently trending on high-performance finance shorts. It provides immediate, actionable value which drives high 'Save' and 'Share' counts.
sources: Chris Voss - Never Split the Difference (Mirroring Technique)

ideas.title: The Red Tag Scam
ideas.angle: A visual demonstration showing how your brain bypasses logic when it sees the color red on a price tag, even if there is no actual discount. It triggers the 'Survival Brain' to buy before investigating. Comment trigger: 'Have you ever bought something just because it was red?'
ideas.reason: This idea leverages a 'hidden truth' about everyday environments (supermarkets), creating a high 'Curiosity Gap.' It falls under the 'Insane Money Secrets' archetype which typically sees >100% APV due to the 'shock' reveal.
sources: Psychology of Color in Marketing - University of Winnipeg
Journal of Retailing - The effect of price-color congruency
